description: We are Acesso +, a team passionate about technology, innovation, and solving real-world problems. Our skills include web development, UI/UX, design, and creative thinking. We believe in the power of technology and data to turn challenges into impactful solutions. We welcome collaborators with experience or interest in data science, remote sensing, geography, data analysis, and software development who are eager to learn, collaborate, and build something meaningful.
summary: Acesso+ Climate Intelligence is a national, multi-region Earth observation platform for Mozambique built around NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band SAR (GCOV) data and complementary satellite sources. Scattered data catalogs, cloud cover over optical imagery, and incompatible spatial/temporal scales often delay flood assessment and create false certainty when observations are missing. Our platform indexes verified NISAR coverage across Mozambique, supports pre-, during-, and post-event analysis over any covered area of interest, separates permanent water from flood signals, and highlights potentially exposed infrastructure and population without inventing missing data. By pairing windowed remote streaming with explicit source auditing, deterministic plain-language summaries, and offline demo resilience, it helps civil protection, humanitarian teams, and researchers evaluate flood evidence transparently.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Acesso+ Climate Intelligence is a national monitoring, multi-event flood analysis, and potential exposure platform for Mozambique anchored on verified NISAR GCOV coverage. Rather than assuming coverage or treating missing observations as zero, the system queries metadata catalogs to verify available orbital passes (894 GCOV footprints indexed over Mozambique, checks sensor compatibility (track, orbit direction, frame, polarization, grid, and CRID), and streams only windowed subsets of remote data. Users can browse national coverage, inspect observations by source and date, analyze events across provinces/districts or custom AOIs, compare pre/event/post passes, separate permanent water from flood signals on a cell grid, and inspect potential exposure alongside explicit limitations and deterministic summaries.

What benefits does it have?

- Scientific rigor over speculative alerts: distinguishes raw radar/optical signals, inference, and confirmation.

- Explicit handling of no_data, partial coverage, cloud obstruction, and incompatible CRIDs.

- Bandwidth-efficient windowed streaming instead of downloading multi-gigabyte granules.

- Full offline demonstration mode using local snapshots so field or hackathon demos remain reliable without live external APIs.

What is the intended impact of the project?

To empower civil protection, humanitarian organizations, researchers, and territorial planners in Mozambique with traceable, transparent Earth observation evidence for flood monitoring and potential exposure assessment—without presenting unvalidated signals as confirmed physical damage.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

- Languages & Runtime: Python, TypeScript / JavaScript.

- Geospatial & Data Processing Worker: earthaccess, h5py, rasterio, xarray, geopandas, numpy.

- Frontend, API & Storage: Next.js, Leaflet, MongoDB, Docker.

- Case Study & Demo Workflow: Technical demonstration on Limpopo Floods — Gaza (January 2026), Track 114 Ascending, Frame 165.

How is your project creative and what factors did your team consider?

Instead of building a black-box risk score or decorative multi-source dashboard, we designed a rules-based evidence engine and source-audit workflow tailored to real operational constraints in Mozambique. Key design factors included preventing false certainty from cloud cover or missing passes, enforcing CRID compatibility before dB comparisons, separating permanent water (JRC / dry reference) from flood signals, evaluating cells independently without interpolation, and keeping external official alert integrations (such as INAM) out of scope for this phase.
